description: In ancient mining, wooden scaffolding and timber frameworks were used to give miners access to steep quarry faces, deep shafts, and underground galleries while also supporting the surrounding rock. Platforms, ladders, beams, and braces allowed workers to cut ore or stone at different heights, haul material, and move tools through confined spaces. In deeper mines, timbering could also reinforce unstable tunnels and shaft walls, reducing the risk of collapse and making large-scale extraction safer and more organized.
